scope: Generic TXV walk-in cooler; receiver configuration explicitly changes subcooling interpretation.
reference_policy: Use component-manufacturer diagnostic patterns only within their stated system/configuration context.
Preserve measured values when no applicable classification target exists.
Do not use a packaged-system subcooling target as a universal receiver-system charging target.

domains.condition: Evaporator receives less refrigerant than load requires.
supporting_patterns: low suction/low evaporating temperature when context supports it
look_alikes: flash gas/lack of liquid at TXV inlet
discriminators: subcooling/liquid condition interpreted at the correct physical location
domains.diagnosis_policy: High SH can establish starvation but does not identify root cause by itself.

supporting_patterns: low subcooling when an applicable target/location exists
look_alikes: upstream liquid-line restriction can produce flash gas/starvation
receiver-system liquid inventory can make condenser-outlet SC misleading if interpreted like a packaged condenser
discriminators: localized restriction checks before adding refrigerant
domains.diagnosis_policy: Do not diagnose/add refrigerant from high SH alone. Low-SC evidence is useful only when the reference and measurement location apply.

domains.condition: Pressure/temperature change or obstruction reduces liquid supply downstream.
supporting_patterns: localized temperature or pressure change across drier/component
discriminators: compare upstream/downstream component temperatures; pressure where access exists
check liquid condition/subcooling at condenser outlet and TXV inlet when applicable
domains.diagnosis_policy: Localized evidence is required before naming a specific restriction.

domains.condition: TXV does not supply required refrigerant flow.
domains.diagnosis_policy: Local TXV evidence is required before calling the valve faulty.

receiver_caveat.rule: A receiver changes how subcooling is interpreted.
receiver_caveat.reason: At the liquid/vapor surface in a receiver refrigerant is saturated. Subcooling can occur after a solid liquid column forms and is cooled downstream. Therefore a generic condenser-outlet SC target must not automatically be treated as a universal receiver-system charging target.
